body:
다음 글의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?
A Picture Is Worth a Thousand Words Paul is a comic writer. He has been drawing many comics about overcoming challenges in communication, and it all began with his experience at the hospital with his mother, Anna. A few years ago, doctors told Anna that she had Parkinson's disease. It is a progressive disease which affects the nervous system. It makes muscles shake and gradually become stiff. Over the years, Anna's health got worse and worse. She could not move her body and she was hospitalized many times. Most of all, communication with other people got harder as she lost control of the muscles of her mouth. It took a long time to understand what she was trying to say. In addition, her body was off balance, making her head and back lean to the side. This meant that she couldn't sleep well due to pain, and that she sometimes fell out of her bed. A Picture Is Worth a Thousand Words Paul is a comic writer. He has been drawing many comics about overcoming challenges in communication, and it all began with his experience at the hospital with his mother, Anna. A few years ago, doctors told Anna that she had Parkinson's disease. It is a progressive disease which affects the nervous system. It makes muscles shake and gradually become stiff. Over the years, Anna's health got worse and worse. She could not move her body and she was hospitalized many times. Most of all, communication with other people got harder as she lost control of the muscles of her mouth. It took a long time to understand what she was trying to say. In addition, her body was off balance, making her head and back lean to the side. This meant that she couldn't sleep well due to pain, and that she sometimes fell out of her bed. Paul was there to help his mother. However, every time he had to leave the hospital, he was worried about her falling off the bed and hurting herself.

solution: ⓐ titling (X) → titled (O): 만화(comic)는 제목이 붙여진 수동의 대상이므로 과거분사 titled가 와야 한다. ⓑ walked (X) → walking (O): 주어(she)가 직접 걷는 능동/동시동작의 분사구문이므로 현재분사 walking이 와야 한다. ⓒ to see (X) → to be seen (O): 그녀 자신이 다른 사람들에게 '~로 보여지기를' 원하는 것이므로 수동형 부정사 to be seen이 와야 한다. ⓓ who tries (O): 선행사가 사람(an individual)이고 단수이므로 주격 관계대명사 who와 단수동사 tries가 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓔ giving (X) → to give (O): lead + 목적어 + to부정사 5형식 구문이므로 목적격 보어 자리에 to give가 와야 한다.

A few years ago, doctors told Anna that she had Parkinson’s disease. It is a progressive disease which affects the nervous system. It makes muscles shake and gradually become stiff. 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 할 때, 아래의
[조건]에 맞추어 영작하시오.
He posted the note up on the wall above Anna’s bed and then went home to get some sleep. The next morning when he got back to the hospital, he noticed that Anna’s head had been supported with pillows just like the picture in the note. It seemed that the nurse had seen the picture and helped Anna. Anna slept comfortably and she was, most importantly of all, safe. This was the first comic Paul drew at the hospital, and he was surprised to see how well it worked. Realizing the potential of comics, Paul decided to ask Anna if there was anything she wanted to say to people. He sat down with her and asked her what comics he should draw. He patiently listened to her until he made sure he understood what she wanted. Finally, she asked Paul to draw a comic titled “Anna’s Goal.” In the comic, she wanted to look healthy, walking with her walker. She did not want herself to be seen as just another sick old lady in a hospital bed. Looking at this picture, the people around her began to think of her not just as a patient but as an individual who tries hard to achieve her goal. It led people around her, including hospital staff members, other patients, and visitors to give words of encouragement and support whenever they saw her. Paul and Anna still face challenges. However, comics have been a great help in overcoming them. Comics can be powerful communication tools that take complex ideas and communicate them in a simple and efficient way. There is an old saying, “A picture is worth a thousand words.” Paul’s story shows that words and pictures work well together to tell stories, to communicate with others, to bring out kindness, and to create personal connections. 1회차 실전 모의고사
조건 1. 아래에 제시된 단어들을 모두 한 번씩만 사용 하여 배열할 것.

4. 주격 관계대명사 that과 동사 enable의 어법 (enable + 목적어 + to 부정사)을 반드시 적용 하여 문장을 구성할 것.
보기 a / act / as / comics / communication / connections / enable / people / personal / powerful / that / to / tool / create
→ _____ .
answer: Comics act as a powerful communication tool that enables people to create personal connections.
solution: 문장을 배열할 때 주어는 Comics이고 동사는 ~로 작용하다라는 뜻의 act as를 사용한다. 그 뒤에 보어인 a powerful communication tool이 오고, 이를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사 that절 3인칭 단수이므로 제시된 단어 enable → enables로 변형하는 것이 핵심 형태 변형 조건이다. 마지막으로 enable 동사의 어법인 'enable + 목적어 + to 부정사' 구조를 적용하여 enables people to create personal connections로 뒷부분을 완성하면 모든 조건(단어 수 14개, 1개 단어 변형, 문장 배열)을 충족하는 완벽한 영작이 된다.

He patiently listened to her until he made sure he understood what she wanted. Finally, she asked Paul to draw a comic titled “Anna’s Goal.” In the comic, she wanted to look healthy, walking with her walker. She did not want herself to be seen as just another sick old lady in a hospital bed. Looking at this picture, the people around her began to think of her not just as a patient but as an individual who tries hard to achieve her goal. It led people around her, including hospital staff members, other patients, and visitors, to give words of encouragement and support whenever they saw her. Paul and Anna still face challenges. However, comics have been a great help in overcoming them. Comics can be powerful communication tools that take complex ideas and communicate them in a simple and efficient way. There is an old saying, “A picture is worth a thousand words.” Paul’s story shows that words and pictures work well together to tell stories, to communicate with others, to bring out kindness, and to create personal connections. 다음 글을 읽고 추론할 수 없는 것은?
Paul is a comic writer. He has been drawing many comics about overcoming challenges in communication, and it all began with his experience at the hospital with his mother, Anna. A few years ago, doctors told Anna that she had Parkinson’s disease. It is a progressive disease which affects the nervous system. It makes muscles shake and gradually become stiff. Over the years, Anna’s health got worse and worse. She could not move her body and she was hospitalized many times. Most of all, communication with other people got harder as she lost control of the muscles of her mouth. It took a long time to understand what she was trying to say. In addition, her body was off balance, making her head and back lean to the side. This meant that she couldn’t sleep well due to pain, and that she sometimes fell out of her bed. Paul was there to help his mother. However, every time he had to leave the hospital, he was worried about her falling off the bed and hurting herself. Whenever he left the hospital, Paul wanted to ask for extra care for the discomfort and danger this symptom might bring. However, every time Anna was newly hospitalized, different staff members took care of her, and they did not know about her unusual posture and its problems. Paul was tired of having to explain the situation to each staff member every time. Instead, he posted a note explaining that Anna’s bent posture can be potentially dangerous. It also explained how to set up pillows to prevent her from falling off the bed. But people did not seem to notice it. He felt there was no one but him who could really take care of his mother.
solution: ④ 사람들이 메모를 눈치채지 못했다고만 쓰여 있을 뿐 메모가 너무 길거나 복잡해서 읽지 못했다는 구체적인 이유는 지문에서 전혀 추론할 수 없다. ① 직원들이 수시로 바뀌어 특이 사항을 몰랐다는 점에서 표준화된 병원 절차가 개인 맞춤형 돌봄을 제공하지 못했음을 추론할 수 있다. ② 입원할 때마다 담당자가 바뀌어 상태를 매번 설명해야 했던 상황에서 일관된 돌봄의 어려움을 추론할 수 있다. ③ 자신만이 어머니를 돌볼 수 있다고 느낀 부분에서 Paul의 강한 책임감을 추론할 수 있다. ⑤ 근육이 뻣뻣해지고 수면을 취하지 못하는 등의 묘사에서 파킨슨병이 일상생활에 심각한 영향을 미쳤음을 알 수 있다.

body:
다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
Frustrated, he went to get some fresh air. As he walked towards the elevator, he noticed a sign that said “DANGER” with an image of a person slipping on water. The sign warned people of the slippery floor with both a word and an image. All of a sudden, it occurred to Paul that comics could help. He was a comic writer after all! Using both words and pictures would surely help explain Anna’s unusual posture and how to help her. Right away, he drew a comic consisting of a picture and a message on a piece of paper. He posted the note up on the wall above Anna’s bed and then went home to get some sleep. The next morning when he got back to the hospital, he noticed that Anna’s head had been supported with pillows just like the picture in the note. It seemed that the nurse had seen the picture and helped Anna. Anna slept comfortably and she was, most importantly of all, safe. This was the first comic Paul drew at the hospital, and he was surprised to see how well it worked. Realizing the potential of comics, Paul decided to ask Anna if there was anything she wanted to say to people. He sat down with her and asked her what comics he should draw. He patiently listened to her until he made sure he understood what she wanted.
solution: ④ 다음 날 아침 Anna의 머리가 그림과 똑같이 베개로 받쳐져 있었고 간호사가 그림을 보고 Anna를 도운 것 같았다고 명시되어 있으므로 이해하지 못해 돕지 못했다는 설명은 본문의 내용과 일치하지 않는다. ① 엘리베이터 쪽으로 걸어가다 누군가 물에 미끄러지는 그림이 있는 위험 표지판을 발견했다고 첫 단락에 서술되어 있다. ② 표지판이 글과 그림을 모두 사용한 것을 보고 자신이 만화 작가라는 사실과 함께 만화가 도움이 될 것이라는 아이디어를 떠올렸다. ③ 첫 번째 만화가 그려진 메모를 Anna의 침대 위 벽에 붙였다고 두 번째 단락 첫 줄에 나와 있다. ⑤ 만화의 잠재력을 깨닫고 Anna에게 사람들에게 하고 싶은 말이 있는지 묻기로 결심했다고 마지막 단락에 정확히 언급되어 있다. 천재(조) Special Lesson 실전 모의고사 3회차

Paul이 종이에 그린 첫 번째 만화는 Anna의 침대 위쪽 벽 에 붙여졌다.

body:
밑줄 친 단어의 영영 풀이로 맞는 것은?
Whenever he left the hospital, Paul wanted to ask for extra care for the discomfort and danger this symptom might bring. However, every time Anna was newly hospitalized, different staff members took care of her, and they did not know about her unusual posture and its problems. Paul was tired of having to explain the situation to each staff member every time. Instead, he posted a note explaining that Anna’s bent posture can be potentially dangerous. It also explained how to set up pillows to prevent her from falling off the bed. But people did not seem to notice it. He felt there was no one but him who could really take care of his mother.
solution: ②의 symptom은 “질병이 있음을 보여 주는 신체적 증상” 이라는 뜻으로, 제시된 영영 풀이가 알맞다. 반면 나머지는 모두 뜻이 잘못 연결되었다. ① discomfort는 ‘불편함, 통증’이라는 뜻인데, 제시된 풀이는 ‘편안함’의 의미이므로 틀렸다. ③ posture는 ‘자세, 몸의 자세’를 의미하지만, 제시된 풀이는 ‘약’의 의미이므로 틀렸다. ④ post는 이 글에서 ‘게시하다, 붙이다’의 의미로 사용되었는데, 제시된 풀이는 ‘떼어 내다’의 의미이므로 틀렸다. ⑤ potentially는 ‘잠재적으로, 어쩌면’이라는 뜻이지만, 제시된 풀이는 ‘절대로 불가능한’의 의미이므로 틀렸다.
source: 영어플랫 · 천재(조) Special Lesson 실전 모의고사
choices: discomfort: a pleasant feeling of physical relaxation
symptom: a physical sign that shows a person has a disease
posture: a medicine used to treat serious illnesses
post: to remove a note or sign from a wall
potentially: in a way that is completely impossible or unlikely

body:
다음 글을 읽고 대답할 수 없는 질문은?
He posted the note up on the wall above Anna’s bed and then went home to get some sleep. The next morning when he got back to the hospital, he noticed that Anna’s head had been supported with pillows just like the picture in the note. It seemed that the nurse had seen the picture and helped Anna. Anna slept comfortably and she was, most importantly of all, safe. This was the first comic Paul drew at the hospital, and he was surprised to see how well it worked. Realizing the potential of comics, Paul decided to ask Anna if there was anything she wanted to say to people. He sat down with her and asked her what comics he should draw. He patiently listened to her until he made sure he understood what she wanted. Finally, she asked Paul to draw a comic titled “Anna’s Goal.” In the comic, she wanted to look healthy, walking with her walker. She did not want herself to be seen as just another sick old lady in a hospital bed. Looking at this picture, the people around her began to think of her not just as a patient but as an individual who tries hard to achieve her goal. It led people around her, including hospital staff members, other patients, and visitors to give words of encouragement and support whenever they saw her. Paul and Anna still face challenges. However, comics have been a great help in overcoming them. Comics can be powerful communication tools that take complex ideas and communicate them in a simple and efficient way. There is an old saying, “A picture is worth a thousand words.” Paul’s story shows that words and pictures work well together to tell stories, to communicate with others, to bring out kindness, and to create personal connections.

Frustrated, he went to get some fresh air. As he walked towards the elevator, he noticed a sign that said "DANGER" with an image of a person slipping on water. The sign warned people of the slippery floor with both a word and an image. All of a sudden, it occurred to Paul that comics could help. He was a comic writer after all! Using both words and pictures would surely help explain Anna's unusual posture and how to help her. Right away, he drew a comic (A) [consisting / consisted] of a picture and a message on a piece of paper. He posted the note up on the wall above Anna's bed and then went home to get some sleep. The next morning when he got back to the hospital, he noticed that Anna's head had been (B) [support / supported] with pillows just like the picture in the note. It seemed that the nurse had seen the picture and helped Anna. Anna slept comfortably and she was, most importantly of all, safe. This was the first comic Paul drew at the hospital, and he was surprised (C) [see / to see] how well it worked.

(C) Realizing the potential of comics, Paul decided to ask Anna if there was anything she wanted to say to people. He sat down with her and asked her what comics he should draw. He patiently listened to her until he made sure he understood what she wanted.
solution: 주어진 글에서 Paul이 병실 벽에 붙여둔 첫 번째 만화가 간호사의 올바른 조치를 이끌어내어 놀랍게 성공했다는 내용이 제시된다. (C) 이러한 첫 성공을 통해 만화의 잠재력을 깨닫고 어머니에게 사람들에게 전하고 싶은 말이 있는지 물어보며 무엇을 그려야 할지 귀를 기울이는 (C)가 이어지는 것이 자연스럽다. 다음 글의 다음에 이어질 내용으로 가장 적절한 것은?
Paul is a comic writer. He has been drawing many comics about overcoming challenges in communication, and it all began with his experience at the hospital with his mother, Anna. A few years ago, doctors told Anna that she had Parkinson's disease. It is a progressive disease which affects the nervous system. It makes muscles shake and gradually become stiff. Over the years, Anna's health got worse and worse. She could not move her body and she was hospitalized many times. Most of all, communication with other people got harder as she lost control of the muscles of her mouth. It took a long time to understand what she was trying to say. In addition, her body was off balance, making her head and back lean to the side. This meant that she couldn't sleep well due to pain, and that she sometimes fell out of her bed. Paul was there to help his mother. However, every time he had to leave the hospital, he was worried about her falling off the bed and hurting herself.
solution: 윗글의 마지막 문장에서 Paul이 병원을 떠날 때마다 어머니가 침대에서 떨어져 다칠까 봐 걱정했다고 언급하며 글이 마무리되므로, 이어질 내용으로는 Paul이 그 문제를 해결하기 위해 취한 조치가 가장 적절하다. ②가 오답인 이유: 본문은 의료 기술의 발전을 다루지 않으며, 이어질 내용으로 연결될 근거가 없다. ③이 오답인 이유: 본문은 Anna와 다른 환자들 간의 소통이 아니라 가족과의 소통 어려움을 다루고 있다. ④가 오답인 이유: 파킨슨병의 발병 원인이나 유전적 요인은 본문에서 전혀 언급되지 않는다. ⑤가 오답인 이유: Paul의 어린 시절 이야기는 본문의 흐름과 무관하며 이어질 내용으로 연결될 근거가 없다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 his art could build a visible bridge over the communication gap이 글에서 의미 하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
Frustrated, he went to get some fresh air. As he walked towards the elevator, he noticed a sign that said “DANGER” with an image of a person slipping on water. The sign warned people of the slippery floor with both a word and an image. All of a sudden, it occurred to Paul that comics could help. He was a comic writer after all! He realized that his art could build a visible bridge over the communication gap. Right away, he drew a comic consisting of a picture and a message on a piece of paper. He posted the note up on the wall above Anna’s bed and then went home to get some sleep. The next morning when he got back to the hospital, he noticed that Anna’s head had been supported with pillows just like the picture in the note. It seemed that the nurse had seen the picture and helped Anna. Anna slept comfortably and she was, most importantly of all, safe. This was the first comic Paul drew at the hospital, and he was surprised to see how well it worked. Realizing the potential of comics, Paul decided to ask Anna if there was anything she wanted to say to people. He sat down with her and asked her what comics he should draw. He patiently listened to her until he made sure he understood what she wanted.
solution: ① 뒷 문장에서 '메시지와 그림을 포함하는 만화를 그렸다' 는 내용을 미루어 보았을 때, 글과 이미지가 결합된 만화를 그리는 것이 어머니의 필요를 병원 직원들에게 효과적으로 전달해 줄 것이라는 의미가 가장 적절하다.

removing the physical barriers in the hospital would make Anna's movement easier
posting warning signs everywhere would prevent people from slipping on the floor

A Picture Is Worth a Thousand Words Paul is a comic writer. He has been drawing many comics about ⓐovercoming challenges in communication, and it all began with his experience at the hospital with his mother, Anna. A few years ago, doctors told Anna that she had Parkinson’s disease. It is a progressive disease which affects the nervous system. It makes muscles shake and gradually become stiff. Over the years, Anna’s health got worse and worse. She could not move her body and she was hospitalized many times. Most of all, communication with other people got harder as she ⓑgained control of the muscles of her mouth. It took a long time to understand what she was trying to say. In addition, her body was off balance, making her head and back lean to the side. This meant that she couldn’t sleep well due to pain, and that she sometimes fell out of her bed. Paul was there to help his mother. However, every time he had to ⓒleave the hospital, he was worried about her falling off the bed and hurting herself. Whenever he left the hospital, Paul wanted to ask for extra care for the discomfort and danger this symptom might bring. However, every time Anna was newly hospitalized, different staff members took care of her, and they did not know about her unusual posture and its problems. Paul was ⓓproud of having to explain the situation to each staff member every time. Instead, he posted a note explaining that Anna’s bent posture can be potentially dangerous. It also explained how to set up pillows to prevent her from falling off the bed. But people did not seem to ⓔnotice it. He felt there was no one but him who could really take care of his mother.
solution: 정답: (1) ⓑ, lost (2) ⓓ, tired

Using both words and pictures would surely help explain Anna’s unusual posture and how to help her. Right away, he drew a comic consisting of a picture and a message on a piece of paper. The next morning when he got back to the hospital, he noticed that Anna’s head had been ⓒsupported with pillows just like the picture in the note.
